reasons: The rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, so a document with no solicitation/no-hire/inducement covenant correctly resolves to 'compliant' rather than 'missing'; the finding applies the playbook's classification semantics properly.

The cited paragraphs support the claim: § 5.4 (p0035) only appoints General Managers as liaisons and § 10.2 (p0061) disclaims employment/agency, neither imposing any hiring or solicitation restraint on us.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed — the rendered text is byte-identical to the original, so there is no directional or over-flagging risk.

The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are inapplicable heuristics here: with no non-solicit covenant in the document there is no duration or carve-out to detect, so the regex misses are phrasing/absence artifacts rather than evidence of a defect.

The rationale appropriately distinguishes § 6 exclusivity (competing web projects, and § 6.3's two-year restraint binds the counterparty) as out of scope for this employee-focused rule and beneficial to our party, avoiding a duplicate or adverse flag.
